headline: Max Verstappen controlled a thermal-degradation battle from pole in Sepang, holding off championship leader Andrea Kimi Antonelli to take victory.
whatHappened: Max Verstappen converted pole position into a measured victory at Sepang, executing a two-stop strategy to manage high rear-tyre degradation in intense heat. Andrea Kimi Antonelli jumped Lewis Hamilton off the line into Turn 1 to claim second place and stalked Verstappen throughout, finishing just over two seconds adrift. Hamilton completed the podium ahead of Ferrari teammate Charles Leclerc, while Arvid Lindblad staged an impressive recovery from 22nd on the grid to claim tenth place.
keyBattle: The defining tactical phase came during the second pit window when Ferrari called Hamilton in early on lap 38 to attempt an undercut on Antonelli. Mercedes responded immediately on the next lap, releasing Antonelli into Turn 1 just meters ahead of the Ferrari to defend second position on cold hard tyres.
championshipImpact: Antonelli extended his championship lead over George Russell to 84 points, putting him firmly in command of the drivers' standings with six rounds remaining. Verstappen's win tied him with Lando Norris on 188 points in fifth place, though Mercedes retains a massive advantage at the top.
watchThis: Observe how drivers manage thermal degradation through the sweeping long-radius corners of Sector 2. Verstappen consistently lifted early into Turn 5 to protect his left-rear tyre, saving enough traction for the heavy braking zone into Turn 15.
